entries.whatItIs: A system-verification framework that runs a system in a controlled setup and labels each finding supported, refuted or unresolved, based on the evidence rather than the agent. It allows “nothing happened” or exact counts only after an observable end point, never a timer.
entries.whyItMatters: It adds real-system evidence with clear limits on what a finding covers, next to the replay and mock-model cards. It is alpha, needs a heavy container and tracing setup, and is not installed or run.

entries.title: tapehead — append-only contiguous tape, one writer, repair-by-append, replay-derived context
entries.why: Agent kernel whose single source of truth is an append-only tape; message history is derived by replay, not stored separately (README-pinned concepts; graded from README only — docs/design.md HTTP 404). Frame sequence numbers are position starting at 0, contiguous, no holes; recorded frames never modified/deleted/reordered; single writer per tape; repair is by appending (never editing old frames); streaming deltas never go on the tape — live stream only. mem/fs/db media share Tape/Silo protocols; kernel holds no provider and reads no env vars; host-declared msgspec tool schemas; tool failure returns an error result without aborting the turn. Caveats: ★0, no SPDX license detected → reference design only, nothing copied/vendored; concepts beyond the pinned list still under discussion in issue #1; README partly Chinese; not installed/run here. Overlaps simply / claimcheck / orglet / vnx — general case of those ledger invariants. Patterns/reference, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: tapehead: an agent built on one log that is only ever added to
entries.whatItIs: An agent core design where one append-only log is the single source of truth and the message history is rebuilt by replaying it. Entries are numbered with no gaps, never edited, deleted or reordered, have one writer, and fixes are made by adding new entries.
entries.whyItMatters: It is the general case of the ledger rules behind several other cards, such as simply and claimcheck. Judged from its readme alone and with no license detected, it is a reference design only; not installed or run.

entries.title: gatehouse — GATES.md oracles + evidence binding + --reverify (Stop hook anti-wedge)
entries.why: Stdlib-only Python 3.9+ completion gates: a GATES.md ledger pairs each outcome with CHECK (shell) + EXPECT (marker); a gate is met only when the command exits 0, the output contains the marker, and evidence is bound to the current gate definition (edit CHECK/EXPECT/CWD and old evidence goes stale). --status and the Claude Code Stop hook never execute checks; --approve records each exact oracle in a private 0700 store outside the repo; --reverify re-runs every runnable gate including met ones and demotes failures; Stop releases after six consecutive blocks with no state change (anti-wedge); ABANDON is a handoff, never a pass. Mechanical form of code-decides-done + the 2026-09-25 replay regression check. Caveats (README + pack §5): proves only the oracle you wrote; approval is consent not proof (changed scripts can run under old approval); evidence detects drift not forgery; young ★0 MIT port of Leonxlnx/unlazy gate core (upstream outside recency window — do not treat evidence as interchangeable); not installed/run here. Overlaps published Proof (Stop claim checks) — gatehouse's distinct piece is declared oracles + binding + reverify. Patterns/hooks over existing seats, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: gatehouse: declared checks that decide when an agent's task is done
entries.whatItIs: A tool where each task outcome is paired with a command and the text its output must contain. A gate is met only when that check passes against its current definition, and a re-verify step re-runs every runnable gate, even ones already met.
entries.whyItMatters: It is a mechanical form of our rule that a real check, not the agent's word, decides done, and of our replay regression check. It proves only the checks you write and detects drift, not forgery; not installed or run.

entries.title: skillwharf — commit-sha + content-hash skill lockfile, all-or-nothing sync, doctor + usage
entries.why: npm package manager for shared SKILL.md folders (Node ≥22.12): skillwharf.json + lockfile pin each skill to a full commit sha and integrity sha256; one store copy is symlinked into .claude/skills and cross-tool .agents/skills (Cursor opt-in). sync fetches and checks every skill before installing any — hash mismatch or unpinned entry (unless --allow-unpinned) stops with nothing installed. doctor reports broken links, lockfile drift, folders skillwharf did not create, and stale unused skills; usage reads Claude Code local session logs only to count which skills actually fire (Codex/Cursor have no comparable logs — stated limit). Caps: 2,000 files / 50 MB per skill; refuses write-through symlinked store/agent folders. Complements catstack (prune/freshness) and cinch (dialect matrix) with the pinning/integrity half of seat install. Caveats: ★0 MIT, young; not installed/run here; Windows copy fallback has a forged-links edge case the README discloses. Patterns/checks, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: skillwharf: pins shared agent skills to exact versions and checks them
entries.whatItIs: A package manager for shared agent skill folders. It pins each skill to an exact commit and content hash, installs nothing if any skill fails its check, and reports broken links, drift and unused skills.
entries.whyItMatters: It covers the pinning and integrity half of installing skills on our coding agents, next to the catstack and cinch cards. Young and not installed or run; its count of which skills fire works from one coding CLI's logs only.

entries.title: sessionpipe — privacy tiers 0–3, non-disableable secrets redaction, per-harness conformance fixtures
entries.why: Open protocol + client (npm, pre-release 0.1.x; Apache-2.0 code / CC BY 4.0 spec) that installs hooks for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and more; events land in a local outbox and leave only when a sink is added. Four privacy tiers per sink with receiver max and lower-wins; secrets ruleset runs on every string above tier 0 and cannot be turned off; PII reduction is a separate opt-in; sessionpipe tail shows exactly what a tier would send before you point a sink anywhere. Ships spec/, JSON schemas, and conformance/ with real hook payloads per harness plus a conformance CLI. Three promises: no telemetry, secrets never leave, your server or none. Fit: written 'what may leave a seat' contract for our activity feed (file sink only) + per-harness hook payload reference next to cinch's dialect matrix. Overlap: Agent Console owns token accounting; sessionpipe is event transport/redaction/tiering. Caveats: ★4, pre-release; not installed/run here. Patterns/reference, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: sessionpipe: controls which agent session events may leave the machine
entries.whatItIs: An open protocol and client that hooks into several coding CLIs and keeps session events in a local outbox until you add a destination. Each destination gets one of four privacy levels, and a secrets filter that can't be turned off runs above the lowest level.
entries.whyItMatters: It could give us a written rule for what may leave a coding seat, for our activity feed written to a file only, plus real hook examples for each tool. Pre-release; not installed or run.

entries.title: harness-mocks / claude-mock — deterministic claude binary mock for model-free harness e2e
entries.why: Go monorepo whose claude-mock stands in for the claude binary so e2e suites run without a model call (tip has 19 e2e suite dirs covering hooks, session file, subagent block loop, plugin hooks, compaction, resume prompt, transcript chain, session lifecycle, etc.; make build / test-unit / test-e2e; releases build linux/amd64 + linux/arm64). Direct instrument for the 2026-09-25 replay regression check and for writing Mac hooks (stingray / claimcheck / Proof) against cited harness semantics instead of folklore. Pack collect also fetched a 27.8 KB EVIDENCE.md with per-behaviour evidence tags and a Not modelled gap list; that file is absent from tip main as of this publish (hook-contract detail treated as pack-time verification, not re-fetched tip docs). Caveats: ★1 MIT; external PRs need signed CLA + signed commits; release assets Linux-only; mock not built or run here; token counts / some stream frames called out as unmodelled in pack. Patterns/reference + mock harness, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: harness-mocks: a stand-in coding CLI so harness tests run without a model
entries.whatItIs: A project whose mock stands in for one coding CLI's program, so end-to-end test suites run without calling a model. Its 19 suites cover hooks, session files, compaction, resume and the session lifecycle.
entries.whyItMatters: It could back our replay regression check and let us write Mac hooks against cited behavior instead of folklore. Release builds are Linux-only, token counts are not modeled, and the mock was not built or run here.

entries.title: dsh-stable-context-first — reorder question-independent DSH context for prompt-prefix cache
entries.why: Local DSH plugin (0.1.0-local.1, MIT, zero deps, not published) that registers one agent/pre-step waterfall listener with prepend:true and permutes decision.messages so question-independent injected context precedes the user message — pure permutation (unit tests assert multiset identity, idempotence, no mutation; README reports 14/14). Moves only two allow-listed sources (skill-catalog; dsh-system-prompt runtime-context snapshot) and never moves skill-invocation, agent-instructions, hooks, user message, or system prompt. Documents the DSH seam: options.messages must byte-match session.deriveMessages() or the agent-loop invariant fails with log-reconstruction desync. Author measurements on llama-server / RX 7900 XT: reusable prefix ~67.96% → ~99.8%+, prefill ~17.9 s → ~0.58 s. Fit: only DSH-seat-specific token-prefix lever in this pack; reference/pattern for our OpenRouter DSH collectors. Caveats (pack §5 + README): measurements are the author's local KV cache, not OpenRouter or our seat — transfer unproven; unpublished/local; do not install without a DSH owner + Jev constant-baseline/shadow step. Patterns/reference, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: A plugin that puts fixed context first so more of the prompt is cached
entries.whatItIs: A local, unpublished plugin for the harness behind one of our scout seats. It reorders messages so context that doesn't depend on the question comes before the user's message, moving only two approved sources and never the system prompt.
entries.whyItMatters: A longer shared opening lets the prompt cache reuse more; the author measured reusable prefix rising from about 67.96% to 99.8% on local hardware, which may not carry over to our seat. Installing it would need a seat owner, a baseline and a log-only shadow trial first.

entries.title: Proof — Stop hook that fact-checks completion claims with real checks + tamper receipts
entries.why: Claude Code skill + dual hooks: SessionStart snapshots the repo (`refs/proof/baseline/session`); Stop intercepts completion claims ("tests pass" / "all done"), runs real checks (tests/build/types/lint/http) in a 90s inline budget, diffs vs baseline, applies tamper rules (skips, deleted tests, `.only`, gutted asserts), and returns PASS/FAIL/SUSPECT/INCONCLUSIVE with command receipts before the turn can end. Direct mechanical layer on code-decides-done + Mori done-receipt + the 2026-09-30 claim-vs-record prose lock (claimcheck covers transcript-vs-claim; Proof also re-runs the checks). Caveats: hook entrypoints are `proof/scripts/proof_session_start.py` + `proof_trigger.py` (not `hooks/`); Python 3.11+; headless `claude -p` Stop-hook fire not verified here; overlaps claimcheck (heavier). MIT. Patterns/hooks over existing seats, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false (tamper half already folded as prose on 2026-09-30).
entries.plainTitle: Proof: re-runs the real checks when an agent claims it is done
entries.whatItIs: A pair of hooks for one coding CLI: it snapshots the repo at session start, and when the agent claims “tests pass” or “all done”, it runs real checks, compares with the snapshot and flags tampering like skipped or deleted tests before the turn can end.
entries.whyItMatters: It is a heavier mechanical layer on our rule that a real check, not the agent's word, decides done, since, unlike claimcheck, it also re-runs the checks. Its tamper half was already written into our rules as prose; whether it fires in non-interactive runs is unverified.

entries.title: temper — author-time contract type-checker for Claude Code harnesses (tsc, not ESLint)
entries.why: CLI that validates a `.claude/` harness (skills, rules, hooks, MCP, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) against Anthropic schemas and a declared contract so malformed frontmatter, ignored rule keys, and dead hook paths fail at author-time instead of silently at headless runtime. `npx @dtmd/temper check --harness .`; optional PreToolUse guard + typed harness-as-program emit. Fits seat-sync / install-hook drift across our multi-CLI skill homes. Caveats: npm `@dtmd/temper` 0.0.21 prebuilt binaries are Linux/Windows x64 only — macOS is "next" (needs Rust 1.96+ source build on this Mac today); checks `.claude/` only (not ~/.dsh/Muse/Agy homes); pre-1.0. Dual MIT OR Apache-2.0. Patterns/checks, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: temper: catches broken agent setup files while you write them
entries.whatItIs: A command-line checker for one coding CLI's setup folder of skills, rules, hooks and instruction files. It checks them against the vendor's schemas and a declared contract, so bad headers, ignored keys and dead hook paths fail early, not silently at run time.
entries.whyItMatters: It points at setup drift across our coding agents' skill folders. There is no ready-made Mac build yet, it checks only one CLI's folder and not our other seats, and it is still an early version.

entries.title: cadence-hooks — compiled Rust Claude Code hooks + cadence-obsidian vault rm/empty-write guards
entries.why: Single native binary consolidating 78 Claude Code hooks across 6 namespaces (cadence / git-guardrails / rules / obsidian / metrics / session) with claimed sub-ms cold starts and zero runtime deps. `cadence-obsidian` is the fleet-relevant slice: blocks `rm`/destructive ops and empty `Write` over an existing vault file, plus SessionStart liveness — machine enforcement of forbidden.md vault invariants at PreToolUse. Homebrew install on macOS (`brew install cameronsjo/tap/cadence-hooks`); also cargo/manual per-platform archives. Caveats: LICENSE is Apache-2.0 + Commons Clause (no selling); Claude Code hooks only (does not cover Muse/DSH/Agy/Fable seats that share the vault); "sub-millisecond" is author claim, not measured here; needs `OBSIDIAN_VAULT` set. Patterns/binary guards, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: cadence-hooks: bundled agent hooks, including guards for vault notes
entries.whatItIs: A single native program that bundles 78 hooks for one coding CLI. Its vault part blocks deletes, other destructive commands and empty writes over an existing vault file, and checks liveness at session start.
entries.whyItMatters: It would turn the vault rules in our list of past mistakes into a machine check before each tool call. It covers one coding CLI only, not the other seats sharing the vault, and its speed is the author's claim, not measured here.

entries.title: Context Guard — context-growth ceiling + structured handoff checkpoints before long chats explode
entries.why: Five Python-stdlib Claude Code hooks that measure live context, warn on quadratic re-read cost, force a structured handoff note (`handoff-template.md`) past a ceiling (Stop refuses to close; `CEILING_MAX = 3`), write a stub note if none exists, and rehydrate a memory manifest on the next chat. Pattern fits grok-token-save-cuts + rari handoff-packet for long Coding EM / Field Brief sessions. Caveats: the 800k-token / 54-compaction / 16% savings figures are the author's own 64-session account, not ours; README examples are Windows-first and the author notes it has only ever been run on Windows (cross-platform path bug fixed in tests, not on a real Mac); our fleet runs are mostly one-shot `grok-tmux-run` jobs, not long interactive chats — adopt the handoff-checkpoint pattern, do not assume the savings numbers transfer. MIT. Patterns/hooks, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: Context Guard: forces a handoff note before a chat's context grows too big
entries.whatItIs: Five small hooks for one coding CLI that measure a chat's live context, warn as re-reading costs grow, and past a ceiling force a structured handoff note by refusing to close the chat. The next chat reloads from a memory list.
entries.whyItMatters: Its handoff-checkpoint pattern could fit our token-saving and handoff-packet rules for long sessions, though most of our runs are one-shot jobs. The savings figures are the author's own, the author says it has only run on Windows, and they may not carry over.

entries.title: catstack — symlink+prune install integrity, skill A/B gate, thrash-reflect-automate, hook-freshness
entries.why: `./install.sh` symlinks skills/hooks/rules into Claude, Cursor, and Codex, then removes any link into catstack the run did not create so renamed/deleted skills do not linger — the closest external mirror of our seat-install hole (we copy without a manifest). Ships `skill-ab-token-gate` (paired A/B token proof for skill/hook changes), `thrash-reflect-automate` (FAIL → reflect → fix the class → codify invariant → automate a catch → re-validate), and advisory `hook-freshness` (installed hooks behind checkout). Direct fit for install integrity + the locked-but-unbuilt replay promotion gate. Caveat: GitHub reports no SPDX license — patterns only, do not vendor files. Not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: catstack: installs agent skills by link and removes stale ones
entries.whatItIs: A setup kit that links skills, hooks and rules into three coding CLIs, then removes any link into the kit that the run didn't create, so renamed or deleted skills don't linger. It also ships a paired A/B token test for skill and hook changes and an advisory check for outdated hooks.
entries.whyItMatters: It mirrors a gap in how we install skills on our coding agents, since we copy files without a record of what was installed, and fits the replay promotion gate we locked but have not built. No license reported, so patterns only.

entries.title: chargehand — open_questions unresolved-claims list, Prompt CI paired evals, approval above risk/cost
entries.why: Result contract with an evidence resolver: every claim is checked against files at a commit, diffs, session messages, or caller inputs; unresolved claims move to first-class `open_questions` (the missing machine-readable field in our done receipt). Prompt CI runs paired evals on PRs touching `prompts/` or `presets/` and posts a commit status; preset changes wait for approval in a `prompt-ci-review` environment. Presets can require approval above a risk or cost estimate. Caveat: pre-1.0, workers read-only — adopt the contracts, do not install the runtime. Apache-2.0. Patterns/contracts, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: chargehand: unresolved claims in an agent's result become open questions
entries.whatItIs: An agent result format that checks every claim against files, diffs, session messages or inputs and moves unresolved claims to an open-questions list. It also runs paired tests on PRs that change prompts, and presets can require approval above a risk or cost estimate.
entries.whyItMatters: Our done report has no machine-readable field for unresolved claims, and this shows one. The card suggests borrowing its contracts rather than installing its early runtime.

entries.title: orglet — one catch-up not N replays, per-day schedule cost cap, never-guess failed spend, evidence-ID file hash
entries.why: Schedule hygiene we need written into Manage routines: missed fires collapse into one catch-up you can run or skip while the next slot stays on the calendar; optional per-day cost cap on the schedule itself; if an API request fails or omits usage, the budget reservation is kept and zero is written only when confirmed — never guesses a failed request was free. Evidence IDs on `workspace_read` are checked against grant + unchanged file hash before a report is accepted. Caveat: early software, AGPL-3.0, desktop-app install class — patterns only, no install. Not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: orglet: one catch-up for missed runs, and no guessing about failed spend
entries.whatItIs: A desktop app whose scheduler folds missed runs into one catch-up you can run or skip, can cap cost per day, and never assumes a failed request was free unless that is confirmed. Reports are accepted only if their evidence points at allowed, unchanged files.
entries.whyItMatters: The card says these schedule habits should be written into the manager bot's routines. Early software, and its license and desktop install keep this to patterns only; no install.

entries.title: wordcell — path-scoped vault context, graph proofs tied to source revision, provider-failure keeps baseline
entries.why: Reads an existing Obsidian/Markdown vault in place (no init/convert). Frontmatter `repository_scopes` plus `wordcell context <path>` returns only the notes/plans/scoped AGENTS.md for the path an agent is about to change — the missing retrieval bridge between our Decisions/forbidden.md and the file under edit. Graph proofs are tied to a specific source revision; optional hosted Jev rerank keeps exact-search order as baseline on provider failure with a diagnostic. Caveats: requires Bun; default support discovery notices print to stderr for agents (`HRANESS_SUPPORT=off` suppresses). MIT. Patterns/retrieval, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: wordcell: gives an agent only the vault notes for the file it is changing
entries.whatItIs: A tool that reads an existing notes vault in place and, for the file an agent is about to change, returns only the notes, plans and instructions scoped to that path. If its optional hosted ranking fails, it falls back to plain exact-search order.
entries.whyItMatters: It points at a missing link from our decision notes and list of past mistakes to the file being edited. It requires Bun and by default prints support notices that agents see; patterns only.

entries.title: cinch — SKILL.md dialect matrix, .cinch.json audit manifest, non-destructive exists outcome, cinch diff
entries.why: Author-once dialect bridge: translates one SKILL.md into a multi-harness matrix (README matrix lists 12 incl. Grok `.grok/skills/` with `when-to-use`/`allowed-tools` and unsupported Claude keys stripped; badge says 11). Every run writes `.cinch.json` — exact audit of files written/merged/skipped; `cinch status` checks integrity; `cinch diff` shows workspace drift as unified diffs. Zero destructive overwrites (`outcome: "exists"` for hand-crafted files). Complements catstack (install integrity/prune vs dialect translation/manifest). Caveat: dialect rows are project vendor-doc claims, not independently re-verified here. MIT; uvx. Patterns/reference data, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: cinch: write a skill once and translate it for many coding agents
entries.whatItIs: A tool that translates one skill file into the formats of many agent harnesses, dropping keys a harness doesn't support. Each run writes an audit of files written, merged or skipped, leaves hand-made files alone and can show drift as diffs.
entries.whyItMatters: It complements catstack's install checks with format translation and a record of every file it wrote, and its format table serves as reference data. The table rows are the project's claims from vendor docs, not re-checked here.

entries.title: claimcheck — Stop hook that blocks completion claims the session record contradicts
entries.why: Deterministic Claude Code Stop hook (no model, no network, no API key, no deps; Node 18+) that refuses a claim of completion when the session's own transcript contradicts it: tests ran+passed, commit made, push landed, tag exists (paths/ran/merged opt-in, off by default). Ships measured evals (claim-detection precision/recall, p50 latency vs Node startup, sweep over 1,744 real transcripts), audit mode with a decisions log, and fail-open rules — new checks earn blocking only after measured FP≈0. Direct mechanical answer to the triage objection that kept stingray out of the playbook (Jev call per Stop / no-op without TypeSafe key): enforces code-decides-done + no-exit-while-waiting at zero marginal cost. npm `@allan_nava/claimcheck`; MIT. Not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. In playbook (2026-09-30, Haiyuan-approved) as the claim-vs-record check (#claim-vs-record): a pass/pushed/done claim must match the session record, and a green run after skipped, deleted, focused or gutted tests is SUSPECT. Prose rule only; no hook installed (a Stop-hook trial would be Opus-drafted and blind-reviewed, audit mode first).
entries.plainTitle: claimcheck: blocks a “done” claim that the session record contradicts
entries.whatItIs: A hook that runs when an agent says it is done and refuses the claim if the session's own record disagrees about tests passing, a commit or a push. It uses no model or network, and new checks block only after measuring near-zero false alarms.
entries.whyItMatters: Now a playbook rule: a passed, pushed or done claim must match the session record, and a green run after skipped, deleted, focused or gutted tests is suspect. Written rule only; no hook is installed.

entries.title: ccdrift — silent Claude Code drift alerts from local session logs
entries.why: Local-only seat-health monitor that reads Claude Code transcripts and alerts on silent behavior shifts: prompt-cache ratio regressions, tool-loop cache misses, Haiku on the main thread, effort-level / cache-tier changes, session-start context shifts (system prompt, MCP, CLAUDE.md), hooks failing or silently stopping, request failures, responses cut at the token limit. State in ~/.ccdrift (no prompt/response text kept); macOS launchd schedule; incident lifecycle with Claude Code version attribution. Complements Agent Console (Console measures cache splits on demand; ccdrift alerts when the seat drifts). Caveat: set cleanupPeriodDays: 365 in Claude settings so the first run has history to replay. uv/pipx install; $0, no key. Not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: ccdrift: alerts when a coding agent's behavior quietly drifts
entries.whatItIs: A local monitor that reads one coding CLI's session logs and alerts on quiet changes: worse prompt-cache use, a small model on the main thread, changed effort levels, hooks that fail or quietly stop, and replies cut off at the token limit. It keeps no prompt or reply text.
entries.whyItMatters: It would warn when a coding seat drifts, while Agent Console measures cache use on demand. Free and needs no key; the coding CLI must keep its logs long enough for the first run to have history.

entries.title: finetooth — coverage map, fingerprints/re-stamp, and third-recurrence guards for whole-repo review
entries.why: Whole-repository review as an Agent Skill (single stdlib-Python file; README on master): a coverage map (file→block) that fails if any tracked file is unowned; numbered hypotheses with mandatory verdicts per block; fingerprints (a block closed on old code, or moved finding code, turns check red until re-stamped); a findings register in git; guards from the third recurrence (third same-root-cause finding cannot close without a test/lint/CI guard); tests proven by mutations. Three portable patterns for our dual-LGTM contract without requiring the install: (a) reviewer-stated file-coverage line, (b) mechanical form of VERDICT-on-head-SHA (new push resets), (c) mechanical form of #repeat-lesson (3× → guard, not another forbidden.md paragraph). MIT; works across Claude Code/Codex/Gemini/Cursor via Agent Skills. Patterns/checks, not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: finetooth: whole-repo review with a coverage map and repeat-bug guards
entries.whatItIs: A whole-repo review skill that maps every tracked file to a review block and fails if any file is left unowned. A block turns red again when its code changes, and a third finding with the same root cause can't close without a test or lint guard.
entries.whyItMatters: It offers three patterns for our two independent blind reviews without installing it: a stated file-coverage line, verdicts that reset on a new push, and a guard instead of another entry in our list of past mistakes after a third repeat.

entries.title: coding-agent-guardrails — resident-rules byte budget + declared≠effective loading checks
entries.why: Day-to-day harness patterns from real failures: evidence-before-verdict (show the check ran on the right object before claiming done/passing/empty); two-tier git-guard PreToolUse hook (DENY: add -A/-a/--no-verify/force-push; ASK: reset --hard/checkout ./stash); resident-rules byte budget (20,000-byte ceiling on always-on rules, CI-enforced — add one, compress or demote another); declared≠effective via kit state (rules observed loading with SHA-256, flags declared-but-never-loaded); generated README inventory checked in CI. Two imports fit gaps named this week: (a) byte budget on resident vault policy (forbidden.md grows without a ceiling — enforcement half of #repeat-lesson), (b) declared-vs-effective skill/hook loading in nightly Mac audit (lighter than Model Citizen's ownership journal). MIT. Patterns/checks, not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. In playbook (2026-09-30, Haiyuan-approved) as the byte ceiling on resident policy (#resident-budget): AGENTS.md and forbidden.md may not grow past their 2026-09-30 size; add a line only by compressing or demoting another. Declared-vs-effective hook loading and the git-guard hook were not adopted.
entries.plainTitle: coding-agent-guardrails: a size cap on always-on rules, plus load checks
entries.whatItIs: Harness patterns drawn from real failures: show the check ran on the right thing before claiming done, a git guard that denies or asks about risky commands, a 20,000-byte cap on always-loaded rules, and a check that declared rules actually load.
entries.whyItMatters: Now a playbook rule: our shared contract file and list of past mistakes may not grow past their size when the rule was set, so a new line means compressing or demoting another. The load check and git guard were not adopted.

entries.title: swarm-agent-coordination — merge-batch gate, paths-owned covering the diff, shared-resources register
entries.why: Classified field evidence from 35 days of agents building production software in one repo (1,417 commits, 229 PRs, 159 worktrees, zero inter-agent chat): 85/229 PRs carried a coordination incident — 16 seam defects vs 1 textual conflict ("green lanes are not a green merge"). Mechanical refuses: merge_batch.sh + merge gate (test the combined tree, not the lanes), migration-chain single-head check, per-run Compose identity, shared-resources register (ceilings written down), check_paths_owned (ownership declaration must cover the diff — 63 of 221 did not), branch-base claim checks. Honestly scopes its limit (test stub sharing the code's wrong assumption). Strengthens stacked/parallel EM work on one repo (Pages, SDK): re-run gates on the combined tree before merge; paths-owned must cover the diff; repo AGENTS.md carries a shared-resources register. MIT. Patterns/checks, not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: swarm-agent-coordination: what broke when agents shared one repo
entries.whatItIs: Field evidence from agents building software together in one repo, plus a set of mechanical checks. In the author's data, 85 of 229 PRs had a coordination incident, and breaks where separately passing pieces meet far outnumbered text conflicts.
entries.whyItMatters: It could strengthen our parallel work on one repo: re-run checks on the combined code before merging, require declared file ownership to cover the whole diff, and keep a written register of shared resources.

entries.title: Agent Console — local-first cache read/write/output/uncached token split (Claude Code / Codex)
entries.why: Local-first observability that reads Claude Code and Codex transcripts on disk and splits every session's tokens into cache read / cache write / output / uncached input, plus models, list-price cost, and burn rate ($/hr, tokens/min). Completely local: no telemetry, no update check, no crash reporting (optional OTel/Kong/LiteLLM ingest is off unless you opt in). Apple-signed and notarized macOS builds with attested releases; Node ≥ 22; MIT; run from source with `node bin/agent-console.mjs --open`. Direct measuring instrument for yesterday's cachebeat KEEP and for verifying whether Opus effort modulation actually cuts uncached input — our usage dashboard is still a Grok-side activity/fire proxy. Not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: Agent Console: a local view of where each session's tokens go
entries.whatItIs: A local app that reads two coding CLIs' session logs and splits each session's tokens into cache reads, cache writes, output and uncached input, with models, list-price cost and burn rate. It runs fully locally, with no telemetry, update checks or crash reports.
entries.whyItMatters: It could measure the effect of the cachebeat idea and check whether changing the implementer's effort level really cuts uncached input. Our usage dashboard is still a stand-in built from the chat bots' activity and routine runs.

entries.title: stingray — Claude Code / Codex Stop hook for half-done turns and unbacked wait promises
entries.why: Stop hook that intercepts turns that stop half-done: (1) no_action (stopped without doing anything), (2) broken_promise (declared an action this turn's tool calls do not account for), (3) unwatched (promised to monitor CI/PR/build but background_tasks + session_crons + cross-session handoffs = 0). Judgements go to TypeSafe Jev; local count backs shape 3; fixed stderr nudge offers finish / launch a poll / name the blocker. Fails open (exit 0) on every error path so a broken hook never grants less friction. Also ships wrong_language and STINGRAY_SHADOW (log-only, never blocks). Caveat: without a Jev API key the checks skip (does nothing). Enforces no-exit-while-waiting mechanically for Coding EM seats. Claude Code plugin + Codex marketplace plugin; MIT. Not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: stingray: catches agents that stop half-done or make unbacked wait promises
entries.whatItIs: A hook that runs when an agent ends its turn and catches three cases: it did nothing, it claimed an action its tool calls don't show, or it promised to watch a build with nothing set up to watch. It then nudges the agent to finish, poll or name the blocker.
entries.whyItMatters: It would mechanically enforce our rule against exiting while waiting, for coding sessions. Its judgments go to the decision-layer service, and without that service's key the checks do nothing.

entries.title: jev-opus — dynamic Opus 5.5 effort via per-message statements (keeps prompt cache)
entries.why: Runs Claude Code on claude-opus-5-5 and lets TypeSafe Jev (or local heuristics without a key) re-pick effort (low/medium/high/xhigh/max) per step — raise on failing checks, lower once they pass — by passing effort as a per-message conversation statement rather than top-level config, so the Anthropic prompt-cache prefix stays intact. Two modes: `jev-opus claude` (local gateway + "Opus 5.5 · Jev" /model entry) and headless driver via Agent SDK. Default effort ceiling is high (xhigh/max never used unless you raise JEV_OPUS_MAX_EFFORT). Addresses the token burn of our locked CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max default on trivial shell/git steps while preserving peak reasoning for failing diagnostics. Requires Node ≥ 22.18 and Claude Code ≥ 2.1.280; MIT. Wrapper over the existing Opus seat — not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: Raise or lower a coding agent's effort per step and keep the prompt cache
entries.whatItIs: A wrapper around the implementer's coding CLI that re-picks the effort level each step, through the decision-layer service or local rules: up when checks fail, down once they pass. Effort goes inside each message, not the top-level settings, so the cached prompt prefix stays intact.
entries.whyItMatters: Our locked default runs the implementer at maximum effort, which burns tokens on trivial shell and git steps; this aims to cut that while keeping peak effort for failing checks. By default it caps effort at high.

entries.title: Agent Limit Watchdog — 80% warn / 92% stop + weekly reserve before Opus quota walls
entries.why: macOS stdlib-Python watchdog for Claude Code and Codex 5-hour and weekly usage limits: warn at 80%, stop phase at 92%, enforce a 20% weekly reserve (no auto-continue above 80% weekly), reset + 2 min continuation, never auto-buys paid credits. Since 1.4 Claude's 5h stop is a soft stop (deny new subagents/workflows; Claude keeps working + built-in auto-continue); weekly stop / Codex still get the orderly stop (one checkpoint request: status/handoff file, WIP commit without push, workflow run IDs, then pause); set claude_stopp_art=geordnet to restore orderly stop for Claude 5h. Prefer Claude's native auto-continue; night mode only steps in where it fails. Proactive quota-wall handoff before our reactive Opus→Kimi fallback. Zero external deps. MIT. Not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: Agent Limit Watchdog: an orderly stop before hitting usage limits
entries.whatItIs: A Mac watchdog for two coding CLIs' usage limits: it warns at 80%, starts a stop phase at 92%, keeps a weekly reserve and never buys paid credits on its own. Its orderly stop asks once for a checkpoint (a status file and an unpushed commit), then pauses.
entries.whyItMatters: It would hand off before a usage limit is hit, ahead of our reactive switch from the implementer to a fallback seat. The card prefers one CLI's built-in auto-continue, with the watchdog's night mode stepping in only where that fails.

entries.title: claude-code-ops-kit — self-audit + reproduce-first debugging + adversarial verifier
entries.why: Operational discipline kit against silent long-run agent failure: skills/self-audit (claim-to-source table, fact-vs-guess split, double-check that "zero/stopped/missing" claims are not failed fetches or stale checkouts), skills/systematic-debugging (reproduce first, instrument boundaries, one minimal change, 3-strike escalation to a human), agents/adversarial-verifier (separate read-only "assume broken" judge), plus scripts/launchd-watchdog.py for quiet launchd deaths. Directly maps onto forbidden.md "0 items / stopped" false reports and the 2026-09-25 reproduce-before-fix rule for bug tasks. Skills/agents pack only — adapt patterns into ~/.agents/skills/; not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. MIT (master branch). In playbook (2026-09-27, Haiyuan-approved) as the negative-claim check (#negative-claim-check): a zero / none / stale claim needs a lookup that worked, otherwise it is an access gap. Reproduce-first and the adversarial verifier were already covered (rari repro-before-fix, disproof review); no install.
entries.plainTitle: An ops kit against silent agent failures: self-audit and reproduce first
entries.whatItIs: A kit of skills and helper agents against silent failures in long runs: a self-audit that checks “zero” or “stopped” claims aren't failed fetches or stale checkouts, a reproduce-first debugging routine, and a separate read-only reviewer that assumes the work is broken.
entries.whyItMatters: Now a playbook rule: a zero, none or stale claim needs a lookup that worked, or it counts as an access gap. Reproduce-first and the skeptical reviewer were already covered by our rules; nothing installed.

entries.title: Sno Station — shared encrypted memory, peer review, nightly skill proposals
entries.why: Open-source laptop workstation that turns coding agents you already run (Claude Code / Codex / OpenClaw) into one squad: shared encrypted memory in one workspace, agent-to-agent messaging ("Reach"), cross-vendor peer-review skills, and rate-limit failover that picks up with context intact. Nightly RSI loop reads sessions, proposes changes to their own skills, and waits for a human yes — the missing front half of our daily consolidation (20:57 digests write notes but never propose skill diffs) under the rari promotion gate. Cross-vendor review independently mirrors blind dual-LGTM; failover-with-context is a data point for Opus→Kimi handoff state. README is honest: one-command install is "Not yet"; repo is assembled in public (opened 2026-09-18); Apache-2.0; no daemon/cloud required. Patterns/prose only for now — not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. In playbook (2026-09-27, Haiyuan-approved) as repeat lesson → proposed skill diff (#repeat-lesson) inside the existing daily consolidation; no install, no new routine.
entries.plainTitle: Sno Station: one workstation where your coding agents work as a squad
entries.whatItIs: An open-source laptop setup that joins coding agents you already run into one squad: shared encrypted memory, agent-to-agent messages, cross-vendor peer review and a context-keeping switch at rate limits. Each night it proposes skill changes and waits for a human yes.
entries.whyItMatters: Now a playbook rule, inside the daily consolidation we already run: a lesson that repeats becomes a proposed skill change. The tool is not installed and the rule adds no new routine; its one-command install is not ready yet.

entries.title: Model Citizen — stop gate + ownership journal for Claude Code / Codex
entries.why: Control plane under coding agents you already run: write rules/skills/roles/stances once as primitives; it projects them into Claude Code and Codex and enforces with hooks. Verified README features: graded shell-command hook (read-only→irreversible; autonomy stance decides which grades stop-and-ask), stop gate ("the turn doesn't end while your repo's own gate is red"), fresh-context review by agents that never saw the code, ownership journal so every file it touches is recorded and uninstall puts things back, per-session spend ledger exporting over OTLP (off by default). Mechanical form of three locks that are currently prose: code-decides-done as an enforced stop gate, install-agent-hooks.sh drift/revert via an ownership journal, and GYR reversibility tiers as a pre-execution grade. Explicitly not an LLM gateway or replacement runtime. MIT. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: Model Citizen: write agent rules once and enforce them with hooks
entries.whatItIs: A control layer under coding agents you already run: write rules, skills and roles once, and it applies them to two coding CLIs and enforces them with hooks. It grades shell commands by risk and keeps a turn open while the repo's own checks are red.
entries.whyItMatters: It would turn three of our written-only rules into machine checks: a real check decides done, install drift can be undone from a journal of touched files, and the green/yellow/red risk lanes grade commands before they run.

entries.title: cachebeat — inactivity-triggered prompt-cache heartbeat (Claude Code)
entries.why: Tiny Claude Code skill: an inactivity-triggered silent heartbeat that keeps the prompt cache warm while a session sits idle, so the next message reads history from cache (~0.1× input) instead of re-billing the whole transcript. Fires only after true silence, re-arms itself, and self-kills after a deadline (default 8h) so an abandoned session cannot drip-bill. README math: "going cold once costs as much as ten heartbeats." Our seats are idle by design (Field Brief :32, 6h briefs, daily collect) and token-save is a locked priority — a long Fable/Opus EM session past cache TTL re-bills history on the next one-line check-in. Built-in deadline is already a kill condition shape. Claude-Code-only; Sept 2026 note: runs as a background shell task (beat.sh + SKILL.md) after monitors were capped at 30 min. $0, two files. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: cachebeat: keeps an idle session's prompt cache warm with a quiet ping
entries.whatItIs: A tiny skill for one coding CLI that sends a silent heartbeat while a session sits idle, so the next message reads history from cache instead of paying for the whole transcript again. It stops itself after a deadline so an abandoned session can't keep billing.
entries.whyItMatters: Our seats sit idle by design and saving tokens is a locked priority; a long coding session past the cache time limit pays again for its history on the next small check-in. Its readme says one cold start costs as much as ten heartbeats.

entries.title: Gate Inbox — tmux board that surfaces sessions blocked on you
entries.why: Terminal board for running and triaging many AI coding-agent sessions in tmux: one list with live status so the session blocked on you is visible without hunting tabs. Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode run side by side each in its own tmux session; `i` walks everything waiting on you; agents started by hand appear as-is. README: "Gate Inbox reads the panes; it does not sit between you and the model." Our attention routing today is a markdown decision queue swept once at 09:09 PT — this is the live "who is blocked on Haiyuan right now" view that file is missing, adjacent to no-exit-while-waiting and the 540s watchdog. Read-only TUI over existing CLIs, not a coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Small repo (Go). Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: Gate Inbox: a live board of agent sessions waiting on you
entries.whatItIs: A read-only terminal board that lists many coding-agent sessions with live status, so the one waiting on you is easy to spot. It reads each session's terminal pane and does not sit between you and the model.
entries.whyItMatters: Our decision queue is a file checked once at a set time; this would add a live view of who is blocked on Haiyuan right now. It sits next to our rule against exiting while waiting and the stall watchdog.

entries.title: crossagent — dual-agent tmux review with AGREE/ESCALATE/UNPARSED verdicts
entries.why: MCP server (npm crossagent-mcp) that pairs two coding agents in adjacent tmux panes — one drives, the other reviews. Every plan/diff passes through the peer; the reply always ends in a machine-parseable `VERDICT: <word>` with fixed vocabulary: AGREE / ADJUST / OBJECT / ESCALATE / UNPARSED. tmux is the only transport (no network, no shared file, no socket); briefing clears the peer's conversation so the reviewer is genuinely fresh. Gives blind dual-LGTM (Astra+Fable) an interface: today reviewers can return prose we adjudicate by reading; ESCALATE is "only the human can call it" (silent-misroute rule in mechanical form) and UNPARSED detects a non-verdict instead of treating it as assent (retry ceiling schema×1). Adopt the verdict contract as prose/checklist first; installing the MCP is optional/later. Requires Node 22+, tmux, Claude Code or Codex CLI. MIT. In playbook (2026-09-27, Haiyuan-approved) as the review verdict line (#review-verdict-line): VERDICT: APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | ESCALATE @ head SHA; a missing line is UNPARSED and never an LGTM. MCP not installed.
entries.plainTitle: crossagent: one agent codes while a fresh peer reviews with a fixed verdict
entries.whatItIs: A tool server that pairs two coding agents in side-by-side terminal panes: one drives and the other reviews every plan and diff. Each review ends with a fixed, machine-readable verdict word, and the reviewer starts from a cleared conversation.
entries.whyItMatters: Now a playbook rule: each review ends with a verdict line (approve, request changes or escalate) for the PR's head commit, and a missing line never counts as approval. The tool server is not installed.

entries.title: simply — ledger-owned done: judgment to models, gates to code
entries.why: tmux multi-agent harness where an auditor owns the work ledger + verification gates, a Claude Code PM owns the worker fleet, and completion travels a private file-based status ledger. Core rule: "Judgment to models; observation, loops, and gates to code" — agents cannot mark their own criteria passed; `verify` runs the checks and the settle gate stays open until every criterion passes and a QA package exists. Briefs state the outcome + observable criteria, not line-by-line steps ("the model owns the path; the ledger owns the destination"). Also ships max vs low-cost routing profiles (frontier for judgment, cheaper models for research/implementation), which mirrors our Opus-default / Kimi-fallback / flash-collect split. Import as prose + checklist for manage-handoffs and EM intent briefs (mechanical form of the rari promotion gate); no install, no new seat. In playbook (2026-09-25, Haiyuan-approved) as "code decides done": done = a deterministic check passed (tests / file / pushed commit / HTTP 200); self-reports and Jev completion_check are advisory only. Settle-gate/QA-package tooling not built.
entries.plainTitle: simply: models judge, code decides when work is done
entries.whatItIs: A multi-agent harness where an auditor owns the work ledger and the checks, and agents cannot mark their own criteria as passed. Work can't settle until every criterion passes and a QA package exists, and briefs give the outcome and criteria, not step-by-step orders.
entries.whyItMatters: We adopted its core rule: done means a real check passed, such as tests, a file, a pushed commit or a page that loads, and self-reports and decision-layer completion checks are advisory only. We have not built our own settle-gate or QA-package tooling.

entries.title: vnx-orchestration — per-dispatch NDJSON receipts + git worktree per worker
entries.why: Local control plane that drives installed coding CLIs (claude / codex / gemini / kimi / ollama) as subprocess workers, each in its own git worktree, through review gates, with an append-only NDJSON receipt per dispatch (verdict, provider, model, cost). No vendor SDK, so dispatches bill to existing CLI subscriptions (README reports measured cost=$0.0000 receipts). A receipt refuses to call a dispatch done without its PR, and branch protection is declared as YAML with a drift preflight. Patterns to adapt for the EM loop: a per-PR receipts.ndjson line per dispatch/review/merge (the grep-able "receipt complete" artifact for the promotion gate) and worktree-per-lane, so a dual-LGTM reviewer never touches the implementer's tree. Adopt the patterns, not the runtime. The author says it is not a security sandbox, and parallel worktree isolation is not yet race-free. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: vnx-orchestration: a receipt per agent job, each worker in its own copy
entries.whatItIs: A local controller that runs installed coding CLIs as workers, each in its own copy of the repo, through review gates. Every job adds a line to an append-only receipt log with verdict, model and cost, and a job isn't done without its PR.
entries.whyItMatters: Its patterns could fit our coding loop: one receipt line per job, review and merge, and a separate copy per lane so reviewers never touch the implementer's copy. The author says it is not a security sandbox, and isolation between parallel copies is not yet race-free.

entries.title: agent-evals — record once, replay offline; gate on pass rate, cost p95, trajectory, calibrated judge
entries.why: Eval harness that records model calls once and replays them offline (no key, no network, runs in CI), then gates on pass rate, cost p95 (not mean), latency, and trajectory (catches right-answer-wrong-path, e.g. a refund that skips the lookup), with the LLM judge calibrated against human labels (agreement, Cohen's kappa, false passes, order/length bias). Shape for the rari promotion gate + Three-Run Proof trial: replay keeps repeat runs at $0, trajectory checks catch skipped steps, and any Jev/LLM gate promoted from shadow should report kappa + false passes, not a bare score. Caveat from its own README: the same suite scored 92% on replay but 28–44% live (mostly brittle exact-substring asserts), so replay is a regression guard, not proof of live quality. Small, new repo (created 09-23): borrow the pattern, don't add a dependency. In playbook (2026-09-25, Haiyuan-approved) as a light replay regression check inside Three-Run Proof, before skill/prompt promotion or Jev shadow→active; live Three-Run Proof stays the bar.
entries.plainTitle: agent-evals: record model calls once, then replay them offline as tests
entries.whatItIs: A test harness that records model calls once and replays them offline with no key or network, then gates on pass rate, high-percentile cost rather than the average, latency and the path the agent took. Its judge model is checked against human labels.
entries.whyItMatters: We added a light replay regression check inside the three-clean-runs rule, before promoting skills, prompts or a log-only decision-layer gate; live runs stay the bar. Its readme warns replay scored far higher than live, and we borrow the pattern, not the tool.

entries.title: rari (@0xwhrrari) — the Grok Bot operating system: handoff packet, reproduce-before-fix, stricter promotion gate
entries.why: Article (2026-09-03) that splits a Grok Bot setup into model + harness + loop + graph + approval layers, and argues for passing ownership, not transcripts. KEEP 1, structured handoff packet: every new Coding EM kick row and Manage → specialist handoff carries from / to / job_type / objective / artifacts / decisions / constraints / open_questions / next_gate. Manage passes it as the jev-shadow intake state, and Jev packet_complete is shadow only. KEEP 2, reproduce before fix: job_type=bug needs a repro artifact (steps, command, logs or failing test, env/versions) linked before the Opus 5.5 implementer launches; a failed repro parks the kick as blocked with the attempt recorded. KEEP 3, stricter promotion gate: Three-Run Proof stays at 3 runs (their 5-run minimum is skipped) plus rollback tested + receipt complete before moving up the ladder, and the Monday kill review adds weekly bot receipts, one Haiyuan spot-check of a real artifact, and 'would anyone miss this if removed?' → propose kill. Skipped because we already have them: CoS routing, reversibility approvals (GYR), autonomy ladder 0–4 with demotion (identical to ours), bounded retries, blind reviewers, shared-computer-is-not-isolation, and login handoff. In playbook §5/§12/§16 + checklist.
keeps: structured handoff packet (ledger + Manage handoffs; Jev intake shadow check)
reproduce-before-fix for job_type=bug (repro artifact before implementer; failed repro → blocked)
promotion gate = 3 clean runs + rollback tested + receipt complete; weekly receipts + one Haiyuan spot-check + 'would anyone miss this?'
entries.plainTitle: rari: structured handoffs, reproduce bugs first, and a stricter promotion gate
entries.whatItIs: An article that splits a chat-bot setup into model, harness, loop, graph and approval layers, and argues for handing over ownership, not transcripts.
entries.whyItMatters: We adopted three ideas: a structured handoff packet, a reproduction before the implementer starts on a bug, and a stricter promotion gate (three clean runs, a tested rollback, a complete receipt). The weekly kill review gains a Haiyuan spot-check.

entries.title: bounded-agent-runtime — run limits + tool risk tiers outside the LLM loop
entries.why: Hard ceilings enforced by the runtime, not the prompt (max_steps / max_seconds / max_usd / max_tool_calls / max_repeats loop detect), checked before each step and raised as exceptions; risk is a property of the tool (READ / WRITE / EXTERNAL / IRREVERSIBLE), not the agent's self-judgment. Shows how to move our 0xjmori run limits (50/2/$0/0) + GYR tiers from markdown into the grok-tmux-run / watchdog wrapper, with a hermetic model-free chaos test pattern. In playbook as a source pointer beside run limits + GYR (policy already live); runtime-enforced wrapper not built.
entries.plainTitle: bounded-agent-runtime: hard run limits enforced outside the model
entries.whatItIs: A runtime pattern where hard limits on steps, time, spend, tool calls and repeated loops are checked before each step, not left to the prompt. Risk belongs to each tool (read, write, external, irreversible), not to the agent's own judgment.
entries.whyItMatters: The playbook now cites it as a source beside our run limits and green/yellow/red risk lanes, which are already live as written policy. A wrapper that enforces them at run time has not been built.

entries.title: agent-runway — pre-flight quota check before dispatch (Claude / Codex / Gemini)
entries.why: CLI + Claude Code skill + MCP tool that reads remaining quota (% used, reset time) across Claude, Codex, Copilot, and Gemini CLI and returns a proceed / defer / unknown readiness check. Candidate pre-flight before each 6h Opus 5.5 Field Brief launch: route straight to the Kimi fallback when quota is near-capped instead of burning a 540s watchdog timeout. CLI/skill, unlike the UsageBar desktop app we skipped on 09-21. GREEN smoke candidate; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: agent-runway: checks remaining quota before an agent job launches
entries.whatItIs: A command-line tool, skill and tool server that reads how much quota is used and when it resets across several coding CLIs, and answers proceed, defer or unknown.
entries.whyItMatters: It could run before each Field Brief launch and route straight to the fallback seat when quota is nearly used up, instead of waiting out a stall-watchdog timeout. A low-risk, green-lane smoke-test candidate only.

entries.title: CAPO — quota-wall checkpoint + relaunch on the other CLI
entries.why: Detects Claude Code / Codex usage-limit cutoffs, writes a plain Markdown checkpoint of git status + uncommitted worktree changes, and relaunches the session on the other platform; when both are capped it parks until the earliest reset instead of flapping. Maps to our Opus → Kimi / Astra fallback and pairs with no-exit-while-waiting + the retry ceiling. Idea: a "quota limit checkpoint" exception branch in manage-handoffs / Mac launch skill. In playbook as a source pointer beside exception-first quota failover (Opus → Kimi live); auto checkpoint + relaunch not built.
entries.plainTitle: CAPO: save a checkpoint at a usage limit and resume on the other CLI
entries.whatItIs: A tool that notices when one of two coding CLIs hits its usage limit, saves a plain checkpoint of repo status and uncommitted changes, and relaunches the session on the other CLI. If both are capped, it waits for the earliest reset.
entries.whyItMatters: The playbook cites it as a source beside our quota failover, where a capped implementer already falls back to another seat. The automatic checkpoint and relaunch were not built.

entries.title: ai-coding-gateway — PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook to trim noisy tool output
entries.why: Hooks Claude Code's PreToolUse / PostToolUse in ~/.claude/settings.json to strip ANSI colors, progress bars, passing-test lists, and build logs before the model reads them, plus global command allow/deny policy. Adapt the trimming hook pattern only (skip the GUI dashboard) to cut context bloat and premature compaction on long Fable/Opus test runs — a direct token-save lever. Lab card (adapted hook pattern); appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: ai-coding-gateway: trims noisy tool output before the model reads it
entries.whatItIs: Hooks that run before and after each tool call in one coding CLI and strip colors, progress bars, passing-test lists and build logs before the model reads them. It also adds an allow and deny list for commands.
entries.whyItMatters: Adapting just its trimming pattern could cut context bloat and early compaction of the chat history on our coding agents' long test runs, a direct way to save tokens. The card suggests skipping its dashboard.

entries.title: Company-in-a-Box — Jev research_check + completion_check (shadow)
entries.why: unicodef1wn X (2026-09-22): Jev as decision layer between manager and workers with four tools (route_worker, check_research, review_completion, guard_action). We already had route (intake) + guard (pre_tool); added research_check (Field Brief citation: accept|verify_more|reject) and completion_check (before done: complete|verify_more|incomplete) as SHADOW gates (honor:false, never block) plus intake live-worker-menu (available_workers/unavailable). Promote after Three-Run Proof.
entries.plainTitle: Company-in-a-Box: decision-layer checks for research and completion
entries.whatItIs: A social post describing a decision layer between a manager and its workers, with four tools: route work to a worker, check research, review completion and guard actions.
entries.whyItMatters: Our decision layer already had routing and guarding; we added a research check for Field Brief citations and a completion check before done, both shadow only and never blocking, plus a live worker list. Promotion waits for three clean runs.

entries.title: seanswarm multiagents-workflow — dual-read + fail-closed acceptance
entries.why: Skills-only pack (no new seat/runtime): dual-read of the same primary source with a match/addition/conflict table upgrades Field Brief source verification; fail-closed acceptance means prose "done" cannot pass without a mechanical artifact (test/exit-code/screenshot) or independent read-only diff-only review. Complements blind dual-LGTM (Astra+Fable) and CoS verification — does not replace either. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: multiagents-workflow: read sources twice; “done” needs proof or review
entries.whatItIs: A skills-only pack with no new seat or runtime. Its dual read has the same primary source read twice and tables what matches, adds or conflicts; its fail-closed acceptance rejects a prose “done” unless a test, exit code, screenshot or an independent read-only review of the diff backs it.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook: the dual read strengthens source checks for the Field Brief, and the pack adds to our two independent blind reviews and chief-of-staff verification rather than replacing either.

entries.title: orchvia — code decides next step; park unknown outcomes
entries.why: Local Claude/Codex session engine with durable mailbox: "your code and the limits you configure decide what runs next, not a manager model." After a crash, work whose outcome is unknown waits for a human instead of auto-retry — the recovery half of our 0xjmori retry ceiling and the named 09-22 watchdog relaunch-vs-resume gap. Lab card / A/B experiment idea only; no install; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: orchvia: code picks the next step, and unknown outcomes wait for a person
entries.whatItIs: A local session engine for two coding CLIs, with a durable mailbox, where “your code and the limits you configure decide what runs next, not a manager model.” After a crash, work with an unknown outcome waits for a human instead of retrying on its own.
entries.whyItMatters: Parking unknown outcomes is the recovery half of our retry ceiling, and it speaks to a watchdog gap we had named: relaunching a run versus resuming it. Partly in playbook; the engine is not installed and stays an A/B experiment idea.

entries.title: sctxx (+ ccompactor) — model-free session→handoff artifact
entries.why: Reads finished Claude Code / Codex / Pi transcripts on disk and writes a compact provenance-linked handoff any other agent can load (no model calls). Candidate machine-verifiable half beside hand-written vault notes for box↔Mac / EM continuation. GREEN smoke only on non-secret repos; inspect output before filing; off dual-LGTM critical path. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: sctxx: turn a finished agent session into a handoff, with no model calls
entries.whatItIs: A tool that reads finished transcripts from several coding CLIs on disk and writes a compact handoff, linked back to its sources, that any other agent can load. It makes no model calls.
entries.whyItMatters: It could be a machine-checkable companion to our hand-written vault notes when work moves between the bots’ server and the Mac, or continues in the coding loop. Backlog: a low-risk smoke test on non-secret repos only, output inspected before filing.

entries.title: omp-jev-watchdog — instruction adherence + verification honesty (shadow)
entries.why: Shadow-only Jev watchdog that records two checks: observed tool calls vs recent explicit instructions, and final assistant claim vs actual tool results. Mechanizes published CoS clause "evidence ≠ instruction" — detects "command failed then claimed passed." Manual slot-close first; do not install as a blocking gate. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: A watch-only check: did the agent follow instructions and report honestly?
entries.whatItIs: A watchdog for the decision-layer tool we use that runs in shadow mode, recording without blocking. It logs two checks: the agent’s tool calls against its recent explicit instructions, and its final claim against the actual tool results.
entries.whyItMatters: It would turn our published rule that agent output is evidence, not instruction, into a check that catches a failed command later claimed as passed. Backlog: manual checks come first, and it is not to be installed as a blocking gate.

entries.title: livelock + loopguard — named failure modes + loop/oscillation detect
entries.why: livelock names four long-CLI failure modes (crash/hang/stall/api-error) and leaves a machine-readable heartbeat (did-it-finish / what-killed-it). loopguard watches Claude/Codex/Gemini JSONL for loop/oscillation/stall. Extends our stale-only grok-tmux-watchdog (~540s) and pairs with 0xjmori abnormal-volume → stop-and-escalate. Lab card; no fleet replace; appliedToPlaybook false.
entries.plainTitle: livelock and loopguard: named failure modes and loop detection for long runs
entries.whatItIs: Two tools: livelock names four ways a long agent run fails (crash, hang, stall, API error) and leaves a machine-readable heartbeat saying whether it finished and what killed it; loopguard watches three coding CLIs’ session logs for loops, oscillation and stalls.
entries.whyItMatters: They go beyond our stall watchdog, which only flags stale output after about 540 seconds, and pair with our rule to stop and escalate on abnormal volume. Partly in playbook; neither tool replaces our fleet watchdog.

entries.title: loop-orchestrator — tmux substrate + mailbox + watchdog + stateless coordinator
entries.why: Closest external mirror of our grok-tmux-run + stream-json + watchdog + EM heartbeat stack. Portable ideas: lane-readiness classifier + auto-restart watchdog as a named component; coordinator prompt assembled statelessly from files each tick; versioned additive-only substrate contract (CONTRACT.md). Lab card — appliedToPlaybook false (no same-day architecture gap).
entries.plainTitle: loop-orchestrator: terminal sessions, mailbox, watchdog and coordinator
entries.whatItIs: An open-source orchestrator for agent loops built on terminal sessions, with a mailbox, a watchdog, and a coordinator whose prompt is rebuilt from files on every tick instead of held in memory.
entries.whyItMatters: It is the closest outside mirror of our launch wrapper, streamed logs, stall watchdog and coding-loop heartbeat. Noted, with no architecture gap to fill that day; portable ideas include a lane-readiness check with auto-restart and a versioned, add-only contract.

entries.title: bb-spec — mutually-blind agents + disk-docs-only handoffs
entries.why: Hardens blind dual-LGTM (Astra+Fable) + intent/spec/plan loop: implementer physically never sees the spec (only tests), so it cannot teach-to-intent; every stage hands off a file on disk, never chat memory. Complements (does not duplicate) 09-20 portable-llm-council SKIP. Lab card; no new seat.
entries.plainTitle: bb-spec: agents kept blind to each other, handing off only through files
entries.whatItIs: A workflow that keeps agents blind to each other: the implementer never sees the spec, only the tests, and every stage hands off a file on disk instead of relying on chat memory.
entries.whyItMatters: It could harden our two independent blind reviews and the intent, spec and plan steps of our coding loop. Noted only, with no new seat; it complements, and does not duplicate, a model-council tool we skipped.

entries.title: Intent-review stage — third oracle blind to PLAN.md
entries.why: Names EM failure mode: passed plan + passed tests but not what the user asked. Third review oracle checks final diff against verbatim original intent while blind to PLAN.md. Cheap process addition (intent → spec → plan → PR → dual LGTM); no new seat, no infra.
entries.plainTitle: Intent review: a third check of the final change against the original ask
entries.whatItIs: An extra review stage: a third reviewer checks the final diff against the user’s original request, quoted word for word, without seeing the plan. It targets work that passed its plan and tests but is not what the user asked.
entries.whyItMatters: This failure can happen in our coding loop of intent, spec, plan, PR and two blind reviews. Noted only: a cheap process step that needs no new seat or infrastructure.

entries.title: Agent Chaperone — Jev MCP shadow-mode wrapper (backlog/smoke)
entries.why: Drop-in MCP wrapper (agent-chaperone -- <server>) to run TypeSafe Jev in shadow mode on Mac CLI MCP tools without changing servers or adding seats. Lab backlog/smoke only — not install-critical-path. Pair with Archestra 79% constant-trap calibration.
entries.plainTitle: Agent Chaperone: try decision checks in watch-only mode on agent tools
entries.whatItIs: A drop-in wrapper for tool servers that runs our decision layer in shadow mode, watching without enforcing, on the tools our Mac coding agents use.
entries.whyItMatters: It would let us test the decision layer on our agents’ tool calls without changing servers or adding seats. Smoke test only, not on the install path, to be paired with the Archestra calibration card.

entries.title: Foremerge — pre-merge intent/ChangeSet for parallel agents
entries.why: Local-first git-layer intent + ChangeSet declarations catch architectural collisions before merge when parallel Coding EM worktrees diverge on shared interfaces. Lab card; light vault handoff bullet (1-line target declaration) only — tool not installed.
entries.plainTitle: Foremerge: catch clashes between parallel agents before merging
entries.whatItIs: A local-first tool at the git layer where parallel agents declare their intent and change sets, so design clashes on shared interfaces surface before merge.
entries.whyItMatters: It targets a risk in our coding loop: parallel worktrees drifting apart on shared interfaces. Noted only: the tool is not installed, and the only takeaway is a light one-line target note in vault handoffs.

entries.title: Preflight — outbound secret-redaction proxy (backlog)
entries.why: Local reverse proxy that redacts credentials from outbound prompts/attachments before model dispatch. Lab backlog only — do not install. Pair with existing llmtap/cost-proxy backlog (dsh-llmtap-jev-guard-gbdl-2026-09-20).
entries.plainTitle: Preflight: strip secrets from prompts before they reach a model
entries.whatItIs: A local reverse proxy that redacts credentials from outgoing prompts and attachments before they are sent to a model.
entries.whyItMatters: It could keep keys out of what our agents send to models. Backlog only, not to be installed, and paired with the existing backlog idea of a cost-tracking proxy.

entries.title: Archestra — Jev 100-call calibration (79% constant trap)
entries.why: Field benchmark: naive ~75% accuracy can be worse than a benign constant (79% of calls are local status checks). Separate input authority vs output trust in Jev policy rubrics. Calibration KEEP for our Jev decision layer — no install. In playbook (2026-09-27, Haiyuan-approved) as the Jev constant baseline (#constant-baseline): a Jev gate must beat the always-majority constant before shadow→active.
entries.plainTitle: Archestra: why a decision check must beat always guessing the common case
entries.whatItIs: A field benchmark on agent calls: 79% were harmless local status checks, so a naive check at about 75% accuracy can do worse than calling every call harmless. A second lesson: keep input authority separate from output trust in policy rules.
entries.whyItMatters: Now a playbook rule, approved by Haiyuan: a decision-layer gate must beat a constant that always picks the majority answer before it moves from shadow to active. Kept as calibration only; nothing was installed.

entries.title: Portable DSH Multi-Agent Plugin (DSH seat watch/backlog)
entries.why: Scoped to existing DSH seat only: cross-provider review with host-enforced VERIFIED/UNCONVERGED verdicts. Lab watch/backlog — do not add as a new coding CLI seat; dual-LGTM remains Astra+Fable.
entries.plainTitle: A cross-provider review plugin for one of our existing coding seats
entries.whatItIs: A portable multi-agent plugin that runs reviews across model providers inside one existing coding seat, with the host enforcing a verdict of verified or not converged.
entries.whyItMatters: Watch list and backlog only: it stays scoped to that one seat, is not to be added as a new coding seat, and our two blind reviews keep their current two reviewer seats.

entries.title: Closed proof loop (Lingxi / Simon grok-bot-guide)
entries.why: Agents must return checkable proof (CI green, live URL, before/after screenshot) and push back until it matches — not soft done. Applied into manage-handoffs + Coding EM contract.
entries.source: x.ai Grok Bot for Engineering · Xiaohongshu grok-bot-guide-cn.pdf
entries.plainTitle: Closed proof loop: work counts as done only with checkable proof
entries.whatItIs: An idea from the bot platform’s engineering guide and a community guide: agents must return proof that can be checked, such as green CI, a live URL or a before-and-after screenshot, and work goes back until the proof matches.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook: written into the manager bot’s handoff contract and the coding loop’s contract, so a soft “done” is not enough.

entries.title: Weekday specialist ops nudge (Jenny-style 1:1)
entries.why: 08:00 PT Mon–Fri Manage posts playbook bullets + blocker ask into Field Brief / Coding EM rooms so complex workflows do not drift.
entries.plainTitle: Weekday ops nudge: the manager bot posts reminders and asks for blockers
entries.whatItIs: A weekday routine from an engineer’s guide: at 08:00 PT, Monday to Friday, the manager bot posts playbook bullets and asks about blockers in the Field Brief and coding-loop rooms.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as a standing weekday routine, styled on a one-to-one check-in, so complex workflows do not drift.

entries.title: PR board sweep every 12h
entries.why: 09:00 + 21:00 PT daily: scan open PRs (CI/conflicts/stall) → Coding EM Mac CLI unblock + proof. Retargeted from 30m to 12h per Haiyuan.
entries.plainTitle: PR board sweep: scan open PRs every 12 hours for anything stuck
entries.whatItIs: A routine from an engineer’s guide: at 09:00 and 21:00 PT, scan open PRs for CI problems, merge conflicts or stalls, and send them to a Mac coding agent to unblock, with proof.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as a standing routine. Haiyuan moved it from every 30 minutes to every 12 hours.

entries.title: Nightly Mac harness audit (03:00 PT)
entries.why: Overnight rotate one Mac CLI for scoped audit PR on BQAA (or named repo); dual-LGTM; no merge. Morning ping only if ready or blocked.
entries.plainTitle: Nightly Mac harness audit: one coding agent opens a scoped audit PR
entries.whatItIs: An overnight routine at 03:00 PT: one Mac coding agent, chosen in rotation, opens a scoped audit PR on a set repo or another named one, and the PR gets two blind reviews.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as a nightly routine. It does not merge, and it sends a morning ping only if the audit is ready or blocked.

entries.title: P0 urgency mode (keyword-only for now)
entries.why: Documented: saying P0 can mean high-cadence babysit. NOT a standing 5m poller yet — keyword only until Haiyuan asks.
entries.plainTitle: P0 urgency mode: saying “P0” can mean close, frequent checks
entries.whatItIs: An idea from an engineer’s guide: saying “P0”, the top-priority label, can mean high-frequency babysitting of a task.
entries.whyItMatters: Follow-up only: it stays a keyword for now, not a standing poller every 5 minutes, until Haiyuan asks.

entries.title: Shared box ≠ security isolation
entries.why: All Grok bots share one cloud computer (files, browser logins). Treat secrets as fleet-visible. Playbook warning applied.
entries.plainTitle: A shared bot computer is not security isolation
entries.whatItIs: From the bot platform’s docs and a user guide: all of our chat bots share one cloud computer, with the same files and browser logins.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as a warning: treat any secret on that shared computer as visible to the whole fleet.

entries.title: Jev multi-gate router + live session
entries.why: Live session block: mode active, confidence_floor 0.55, OpenRouter typesafe/jev-1.13, jev-route helper, smoke table (intake/pre_*), Manage Bot session recipe. Gates stay; no Playwright.
entries.plainTitle: Our decision layer’s multi-gate router and live session setup
entries.whatItIs: A playbook block for running our decision layer live: active mode, a confidence floor of 0.55, a routing helper, a smoke-test table for its gates, and a session recipe for the manager bot.
entries.whyItMatters: In playbook as the live setup for routing through several decision gates. The gates stay, and no browser automation tool is added.

entries.title: CoS verification — evidence ≠ instruction
entries.why: DSH Lab KEEP (asyncdot CoS): treat every agent completion as evidence, not instruction; re-check live artifact / exit code / published URL before marking a slot green.
entries.plainTitle: Chief-of-staff check: an agent’s “done” is evidence, not an order
entries.whatItIs: A rule kept from the asyncdot chief-of-staff pattern: treat every agent completion as evidence, not instruction, and re-check the live artifact, exit code or published URL before marking a slot green.
